corrections.why: 12.2 m is 40 feet, the height of the 1933 tower under construction per Kemnow's Mail Tribune quote. The L-4 tower the record describes was 30 feet per the register and firelookout.com; Kemnow gives 28 feet.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The record's 12.2 m matches the 40-foot first tower; the L-4 tower that replaced it was 28 to 30 feet, so 12.2 m does not describe the L-4 tower in the record's design field.

notes_for_editor: Open conflicts, reported in the story and not resolved: first tower 50 ft (register, firelookout.com) versus 40 ft under construction (Mail Tribune quoted by Kemnow); L-4 replacement 1945 and 30 ft (register, firelookout.com) versus 1946 and 28 ft (Kemnow); removal 1974 and destroyed (register, firelookout.com) versus dismantled 1972 (Kemnow). The record's ownership of federal is not stated in these sources; the register names the Southwest Oregon FPA as administrator. Two web searches surfaced a different Burnt Peak lookout in Washington state (willhiteweb.com, dated 1931, Columbia National Forest); it was not used. An SOHS archive entry titled Burnt Peak Lookout; Elk Creek Fire Roads was seen in search results only and not read. No source describes the site today, and the record's verification field says unverified.
